tasks.title: Verify LXD is installed
tasks.instructions:
Check that LXD is installed on your system by running:

```bash
lxd --version
```

If LXD is not installed, install it with:

```bash
sudo snap install lxd
```

Then add your user to the lxd group (if not already):

```bash
sudo usermod -aG lxd "$USER"
newgrp lxd
```
hints: If you get 'command not found', LXD is not installed. Run `sudo snap install lxd`.
After adding yourself to the lxd group, you may need to log out and back in for it to take effect.

tasks.title: Initialize LXD
tasks.instructions:
Initialize LXD with a minimal configuration:

```bash
lxd init --minimal
```

If LXD is already initialized, this command may ask if you want to reconfigure. You can skip if it's already set up.

Verify it's working:

```bash
lxc list
```

You should see an empty table with no errors.
hints: If you get a permission error, make sure you're in the lxd group. Run `newgrp lxd` or re-open your terminal.
lxd init --minimal uses sensible defaults — no need to answer interactive prompts.
